posts.cooked:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kq4OlEDiCi8

Remind you of anyone you know?

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
cmschex:

Unless that cowboy travels through time i dont really see that being an issue…even then, comic tropes are not IP enforceable.  I mean, much of the SotM lineup have clear homages to existing characters.

But we are talking about a cowboy bounty hunter with the same hat, cigar problem, shoulder poncho, favors a pistol, uses grenades, and has a robotic left arm.

There is a big difference between playing with comic tropes and flat out copying characters. I'm not saying that Blizzard is stealing Chrono Ranger here, but there is a lot more than just a passing resemblance there. Certainly calls it into question.

McBehrer:

Also, Tracer is Tachyon, Hanzo is like Parse, and Widowmaker is like The Wraith.

These are not even remotely close to the same ballpark as the Chrono similarities.

posts.name: MightySi
posts.cooked:
The same could be said of other SOTM characters themselves tho... Child of millionaires has Tragic Event and fights crime from the shadows while running the Company during the day.  Are we talking about Batman or Wraith? Or The Arrow?  Or Mister Terrific?

Comics characters have a lot of overlap and the very comic-y style of Overwatch is bound to have a few similarities here and there.

Hell, wasn't Jonah Hex a horrifically scarred old west gunslinger who had a time-travel adventure or two a long time before Jim turned up? ;)

posts.name: MarioFanaticXV
posts.cooked:
Wraith is essentially female Batman- she even has Batarangs!

Omnitron X's appearance heavily draws from Mega Man X- right down to using the same font for their names (look at O-X's character card, then look at the title screen from the first Mega Man X game. Same exact font, no mistaking it was meant as an intentional allusion).

I don't know if Overwatch takes inspiration from Sentinels or not- but if it does, then just remember, all art is derivative. As long as no one is saying "I'm the first one to ever have this concept." then those that inspired others should be honored, not offended.
